subjects.displayTitle: The image of God: a dignity waiting to become visible
subjects.introduction: Before anything existed, Bahá’u’lláh writes, God knew His love for us; that is why He created us, engraved His image upon us and revealed His beauty to us. Everything else about human dignity follows from that act of love. The image is not a bodily likeness, since the divine Essence has no form; it is the capacity to reflect knowledge, mercy, justice and generosity, the way a polished mirror receives the sun without containing it. Every soul is pure at birth, and within the handful of dust from which we are made lies a pearl bright enough to light East and West. Yet the image is a calling as much as an endowment: it becomes visible through education, through the mind’s power to penetrate abstract realities, through a second birth into love of God, and through conduct, and a person can also throw this nobility into the abyss and become a prisoner of his own ego. The harsh contrasts with animal existence belong to that moral argument, not to any denial of a person’s worth. Genesis gives the words that are interpreted here, image and likeness, blessing and responsibility within the living world [1]. The journey leads onward to the soul as a mirror, to the divine attributes hidden within all things, and to the spiritual transformation by which an inward possibility becomes a gift to others.
subjects.arc: Begin with universal possibility and creative love, clarify the image, and follow its development through knowledge, character and service.

order.why: Distinguish divine attributes from physical resemblance.
shortened: It is recorded in the Holy Bible that God said, "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness." It is self-evident that the image and likeness mentioned do not apply to the form and semblance of a human being because the reality of Divinity is not limited to any form or figure. Nay, rather, the attributes and characteristics of God are intended.

order.why: Open with divine possibilities present in everyone.
Place love at the origin of the divine image.
Give knowing and loving their central purpose.
shortened: Having created the world and all that liveth and moveth therein, He, through the direct operation of His unconstrained and sovereign Will, chose to confer upon man the unique distinction and capacity to know Him and to love Him -- a capacity that must needs be regarded as the generating impulse and the primary purpose underlying the whole of creation, as mentioned in the well-known sacred tradition.

Upon the reality of man, however, He hath focused the radiance of all of His names and attributes, and made it a mirror of His own Self. Alone of all created things man hath been singled out for so great a favor, so enduring a bounty.

order.why: Keep the transcendence of the divine Essence explicit.
Ground the inquiry in the purity of every newborn.
shortened: Know thou that every soul is fashioned after the nature of God, each being pure and holy at his birth. Afterwards, however, the individuals will vary according to what they acquire of virtues or vices in this world. Although all existent beings are in their very nature created in ranks or degrees, for capacities are various, nevertheless every individual is born holy and pure, and only thereafter may he become defiled.

order.why: Read dignity as a birthright beyond worldly treasure.
Let the pearl image disclose possibility within dust.
Hear the explanation addressed to children.
shortened: O ye young Baha'i children, ye seekers after true understanding and knowledge! A human being is distinguished from an animal in a number of ways. First of all, he is made in the image of God, in the likeness of the Supernal Light, even as the Torah saith, 'Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.' This divine image betokeneth all the qualities of perfection whose lights, emanating from the Sun of Truth, illumine the realities of men.

order.why: Keep the concise definition through divine attributes.
Read divine character in the parallel source.
Consider virtues reflected in human reality.
shortened: According to the words of the Old Testament God has said, "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness." This indicates that man is of the image and likeness of God -- that is to say, the perfections of God, the divine virtues, are reflected or revealed in the human reality.

order.why: Let the mirror gather names and perfections.
shortened: What is the meaning of the image and likeness of God? It means that man will become the manifester of the names and attributes of the Deity; it means that all the perfections and luminosities of the Divine will shine upon the mirror of human beings.

order.why: Keep the perfect mirror’s relation to the sun.
Explains humanity’s likeness to God through the reflection of divine attributes.
Turn the image into a prayer for a polished heart.
Read the human reality through niche and glass.
Continue through temple, throne and horizon.
shortened: O friends of the Blessed Beauty! When the Peerless Lord shone forth from the horizon of "no-place" upon the people of contingent existence, He made the human temple His sacred throne and made the human horizon the dawning-place of His manifest light.

order.why: Retain the image inscribed on the human brow.
Read the praise of humanity’s noble form.
shortened: He created man in the finest mold and with a noble form and majestic temple among the infinite forms in the realm of being.

order.why: Keep the brief statement of the deposited sign.
shortened: O Mu'tamin of 'Abdu'l-Baha! The Supreme Lord has deposited within human reality a most great sign. Some proved trustworthy and preserved this divine trust with the utmost effort and protection, while others proved ungrateful and betrayed the trust - that is, they squandered that gift.

order.why: Follow the deposited gift toward illumination.
shortened: O thou who speaketh the praise of God!

In the essence of man, the hand of divine bestowal hath deposited a gift whereby man may become the dawning-place of the verses of the All-Merciful, and human reality may acquire illumination from the Dayspring of Oneness, and the essence of Adam may become the light-giving lamp of the world.

order.why: Read the comprehensive prayer concerning human reality.
shortened: O my God, Thou hast created creation in countless different ranks and stations, and from among all existence Thou hast chosen the human reality, which encompasses the mysteries of contingent being and proclaims the divine truth in the world of creation. Thou hast distinguished it from all other existence through the outpouring of divine vision, the hidden secret, and the protected symbol, making it a pure mirror reflecting the mysteries of what was and what will be.

order.why: Connect clear expression with hidden human capacities.
Read the signs of divine perfections within the world and human souls.
shortened: When we examine the world and the souls of men, the perspicuous signs of the perfections of the Divinity appear clear and manifest, for the realities of all things attest to the existence of a universal Reality.

order.why: Attend to reason and perception.
shortened: Man is endowed with superior reasoning power and the faculty of perception; he is the manifestation of divine bestowals.

order.why: Keep the reported relation between thought and reflection.
shortened: When in the course of evolution the stage of thought and reason has been reached, the human mind acts as a mirror reflecting the glory of God.

order.why: Read intellectual powers in their spiritual setting.
shortened: God created in us a divine holy spirit,--the human spirit with its intellectual powers which are above the powers of nature. By this he enjoys the ecstasies of the spirit and sees the world illumined.

order.why: Consider the human being as a center of virtues.
Trace discovery, spiritual birth and nearness together.
shortened: God has created man after His own image and likeness. He has endowed him with a mighty power which is capable of discovering the mysteries of phenomena.

He acquires divine wisdom; he searches out the mysteries of creation; he witnesses the radiance of omnipotence; he attains the second birth -- that is to say, he is born out of the material world just as he is born of the mother; he attains to everlasting life; he draws nearer to God; his heart is replete with the love of God. This is the foundation of the world of humanity; this is the image and likeness of God; this is the reality of man; otherwise, he is an animal.

order.why: Connect discovery with making the image visible.
shortened: Then man will make real discoveries, penetrate the mysteries and so reflect them that he will become the image of God.

order.why: Give spiritual education its formative work.
shortened: He must also impart spiritual education, so that minds may apprehend the metaphysical world, breathe the sanctified breaths of the Holy Spirit, and enter into relationship with the Concourse on high, and that human realities may become the manifestations of divine blessings, that perchance all the names and attributes of God may be reflected in the mirror of the human reality, and the meaning of the blessed verse, "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness" may be realized.

order.why: Introduce the Manifestation as an example to emulate.
Make spiritual life a question of character.
Join inward seeking with bodily effort.
Connect the reflected light with actual conduct.
shortened: I hope that this may be so, meaning that the loved ones of God may conduct themselves according to the teachings, counsels and exhortations of Baha'u'llah, so that the lights of the Kingdom may be reflected in the mirror of the human world.

order.why: Read knowledge, love and reliance as fruit.
shortened: Yea, this fruit is the knowing God and love for God, and reliance upon God and is the virtue with which the reality of man is adorned, and it is the perfections which are the great gift for the child of Adam (i.e., mankind) in this first creation.

order.why: Carry divine light into words, action and life.
Use the palace image to examine the effects of deeds.
shortened: That everlasting palace is the reality of man which reality is indestructible. Therefore I am searching throughout the world to find men and women in which the divine palace is completed.

In the heart of every man and woman the construction of this heavenly palace is going on. Praiseworthy deeds and philanthropic actions are the materials with which the palace is built. Vices and the degeneracy of morality are the axes with which the very foundation of this eternal palace laid by the hand of God is uprooted.

order.why: Make the response to creative love explicit.
shortened: God manifested His Love by creating man in His Own Image. Man must manifest the Love of God by developing it in that Image.

order.why: Return to the revealed declaration in its distinct source.
Read the range of purposes attributed to divine creation.
shortened: But the Almighty fashioned man in his own image and likeness for the [sake] of His Love, for drawing the lights of divine virtues, for the manifestation of the celestial power, for the appearance of the efficacy of the Holy Spirit and for the projection of the ideals names and qualities of Divinity.

order.why: Connect the Manifestation’s tribulations with human transformation and peace.
Keep the reported comparison of biblical and Qur’anic language.
Distinguish natural and spiritual realities.
Face the possibility of remaining unaware of the gift.
shortened: Though all human beings are adorned with the garment of humanity, they remain unaware of its reality. This universal gift is manifested in human reality, yet man remains heedless and forgetful.

order.why: Read the criticism of being captive to nature in its theological setting.
Consider the stated limits of material advance alone.
Read descent and renewal through the cited scriptural images.
Confront conduct that contradicts the divine image.
Consider the contrast between noble capacity and self-imposed captivity.
Keep the warning against trading dignity for passing attractions.
Hear humility and the acknowledgment of sin in the reported prayer.
shortened: On the other hand, although man was created in the image and likeness of God and was destined to become the perfect, clear mirror, reflecting the rays of divinity he prayed from the depth of his heart: 'O Lord! We are sinners.

order.why: Read the means of spiritual growth named in the brief selection.
shortened: It is through the Love of God, the Knowledge of God, the spiritual susceptibilities, and the attractions of the heart.

order.why: Keep the promised horizon of spiritual existence.
Connect happiness with orientation toward the Kingdom.
shortened: But I will tell you God has created man after His own image; therefore He has created his condition to be divine, and his real happiness, cheerfulness, wealth, dominion and power, must all be of divine origin, and if he will turn always to the Kingdom he will be in happiness and contentment.

order.why: Let the exhortation to radiance gather the practical challenge.
Return to Adam and the interpretation of divine names.
Distinguish this testimony to the revealed One from claims about ordinary identity.
shortened: and among them are those who have turned towards it and hastened and said: "Here am I, O Lord of Names! I testify that Thou wert hidden in God's knowledge and inscribed in His perspicuous Book."

order.why: Close linked passages with the Báb’s devotional wonder at divine bestowal.
Read the supplied Genesis verse in its own wording.
End with the supplied implication for the spiritual equality of women and men.

questions: What difference does it make to understand the divine image as qualities and capacities rather than physical resemblance?
How do these passages hold together an inherent human dignity and the need for moral growth?
What do the mirror, pearl, and palace images each reveal about potential and responsibility?
What becomes clearer when Genesis is read beside the interpretations offered in this compilation?
How could recognizing divine possibilities in another person change education, friendship, or public life?
Which connected subject would help you explore the movement from knowing one’s worth to expressing it in action?

references.label: 1 · Genesis 1:26–28 · Humanity in the divine image
references.note: Genesis places the creation of humanity in God’s image beside the creation of male and female, divine blessing, and responsibility within the living world. Read these verses alongside the compilation’s explicit interpretation of image and likeness as divine attributes. The biblical passage provides the shared language; the Bahá’í passages develop a particular account of spiritual capacity, education, and character.

subjects.displayTitle: Infallibility: divine guidance and human understanding
subjects.introduction: To call someone infallible sounds like the end of thought, yet in the Bahá’í writings the word opens a set of careful distinctions. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá separates infallibility in essence, which belongs to the Manifestations of God as rays belong to the sun, from infallibility as an attribute, a borrowed light that falls on certain souls and institutions because God guards them from error. The members of the Universal House of Justice are fallible individuals; the body, acting together, is protected. Bahá’u’lláh insists that everyone else is prone to error, and the Báb turns the word inside out: infallibility is not the cautious piety of the religiously careful but the readiness to answer Yes when God asks, Am I not your Lord? The Prophets’ confessions of sin, the Qur’án’s reproaches to Adam and Jonah, laws that change from age to age, all become lessons in humility rather than contradictions. Hebrews offers a Christian counterpart in a high priest who knows weakness yet is without sin and invites the weak to approach [1]. The road leads on to the House of Justice, to the limits of criticism, and to the special knowledge of the Manifestation of God.
subjects.arc: Clarify the principal distinctions, examine difficult scriptural cases, and move toward conferred guidance, institutional scope and continued investigation.

order.why: Examine the fuller account of meanings and grades.
shortened: Know thou that the term 'Infallibility' hath numerous meanings and divers stations. In one sense it is applicable to the One Whom God hath made immune from error. Similarly it is applied to every soul whom God hath guarded against sin, transgression, rebellion, impiety, disbelief and the like. However, the Most Great Infallibility is confined to the One Whose station is immeasurably exalted beyond ordinances or prohibitions and is sanctified from errors and omissions.

order.why: Open with the essential distinction and its institutional example.
shortened: To summarize, infallibility in essence is confined to the universal Manifestations of God and infallibility as an attribute is conferred upon sanctified souls. For instance, the Universal House of Justice, if it be established under the necessary conditions--that is, if it be elected by the entire community--that House of Justice will be under the protection and unerring guidance of God. Should that House of Justice decide, either unanimously or by a majority, upon a matter that is not explicitly recorded in the Book, that decision and command will be guarded from error. Now, the members of the House of Justice are not essentially infallible as individuals, but the body of the House of Justice is under the protection and unerring guidance of God: this is called conferred infallibility.

order.why: Read the unique station in the Most Holy Book.
Place recognition before the acceptance of authority.
State ordinary human fallibility plainly.
shortened: Man is prone to error, for the Most Great Infallibility belongs exclusively to God Himself.

order.why: Distinguish divine guidance from the conduct of other people.
Connect the distinction with an example of concealing faults.
Read the claim of uniqueness through divine unity.
Consider the warning against assigning the supreme station to subordinates.
shortened: The station of the Most Great Infallibility is the station wherein God doeth what He willeth. In that realm there neither is nor hath been any possibility of error. Whatsoever proceedeth from the Source of the Unseen and the Dawning-Place of Revelation is and shall be the truth, and naught else is mentioned at this station.

order.why: Retain the related distinction between the Word and created beings.
Keep the acknowledgment of essential infallibility in its particular discussion.
shortened: Otherwise we are all believers in the oneness of God and acknowledge the inherent infallibility of the Blessed Beauty - there is no disagreement about this.

order.why: Distinguishes forms of infallibility and their relation to authority.
Extend the question to past Manifestations.
Hear the reported appeal to a standard of perfection.
Distinguish capacity to act from desire to disobey in the report.
Keep the further reported account of prophetic purity.
shortened: The substance of the soul of the Prophet is purer than that of the average mortal, it has no traces of ungood impulses, it is aflame with Divine Fire. That is why true Prophets are not susceptible to defilement by sin.

order.why: Examine penitential language as a form of instruction.
shortened: How often have the Prophets of God and His universal Manifestations confessed in their prayers to their sins and shortcomings! This is only to instruct other souls, to inspire and encourage them to be humble and submissive before God and to acknowledge their own sins and shortcomings. For these holy Souls are sanctified above every sin and freed from every fault.

order.why: Read the explicit treatment of scriptural reproaches.
shortened: In brief, the noble Messengers, the great Prophets, the luminous Manifestations, the merciful Realities, the perfect Words, the conclusive Proofs, the brilliant Suns, the shining Moons, and the gleaming Stars - all their luminous inner beings are sanctified from the touch of darkness, and their divine consciences are purified from the stains of vain imaginings. God addresses them thus only for a wisdom, that those possessed of understanding might humble themselves and submit, and abase themselves before the Mighty, the Bestower, and not become proud even if they ascend to the highest chambers, but rather awaken to how the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting addressed the Great Beloved, the Honored Light, the Guide of nations, and the Speaker of the Most Great Name with such decisive address and reproof.

order.why: Place the selected dialogue and assertion of truth within the Book of Certitude.
shortened: Thou art one of the ungrateful. He said: 'I did it indeed, and I was one of those who erred.
Nay, whatsoever proceedeth from these Mines of divine Wisdom and these Treasuries of eternal knowledge is truth, and naught else but the truth.

order.why: Retain the difficult selections concerning Moses rather than explaining them away.
shortened: He said: 'O my Lord! I have sinned to mine own hurt, forgive me.'
Moses Himself, moreover, acknowledged His injustice and waywardness, and testified  that fear had seized Him, and that He had transgressed, and fled away.

order.why: Consider changing religious ordinances through the nourishment analogy.
shortened: In truth, the people of the world have yet not grasped the meaning of "He doeth whatsoever He willeth", nor have they comprehended the significance of Supreme Infallibility. The suckling child must be nourished with milk. If it be given meat it will assuredly perish, and this would be naught but sheer injustice and unwisdom. Blessed are they that understand. Supreme Infallibility, as I once heard from His blessed lips, is reserved exclusively to the Manifestations of the Cause of God and the Exponents of His Revelation.

order.why: Read the change of prayer direction as a further example.
shortened: The True One, exalted be His station, is the possessor of the Most Great Infallibility, and the meaning of the Most Great Infallibility is that error, mistake and forgetfulness have no access whatsoever to that realm. This is the station of "He doeth what He willeth and ordaineth what He pleaseth." If He declares the qiblih to be toward the east, it is the indubitable truth, and if He declares it to be toward the west, likewise. Even as in the Qur'an, the Beloved of all creation, in accordance with the command of the All-Merciful, turned toward the qiblih of Islam to which they turn today.

order.why: Encounter the chronological objection exactly as the source presents it.
shortened: Some among mankind are ever intent upon denial and objection, as evidenced by how the people of the Bayan have repeatedly inquired why the Point (the Bab), may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for His sake, made mention of David, the Psalmist, before Moses, peace be upon Him, when historically David came after Moses.

Say: Fear God and object not to Him Whom God hath adorned with the Most Great Infallibility, His most beautiful names and His most exalted attributes. It behooveth the servants to affirm whatsoever proceedeth from the Dayspring of God's Cause, for none save God is aware of the requirements of His consummate wisdom.

order.why: Connect the claim with divine remembrance and certitude.
Read the word of divine freedom as a ground of assurance.
Keep the assertion that further grades remain to be unfolded.
Examine the Báb’s account of response at the time of revelation.
shortened: Infallibility is not what people imagine in their religious precautions, for when they heard the call "Am I not your Lord?" and did not say "Yea," they went astray. Rather, infallibility belongs to those who, when God said to them "Am I not your Lord?" said "Yea." And God speaks to none except through the tongue of His Manifestation in every dispensation.

order.why: Read its extended citation and application in Bahá’u’lláh’s text.
shortened: In this day certain souls have claimed infallibility apart from God, even as the people of the Qur'an have spoken without understanding and have never comprehended the true intent of infallibility. The ordinance of infallibility is fulfilled today in this wise: every soul who, after hearing the Word of God and His Call, is assured with the word "Yea" is of the people of infallibility, and whosoever is other than this is excluded from infallibility.
Today all people, in whatsoever station they may be, are excluded from infallibility, save those souls who have been assured of this Most Holy, Most Transcendent Manifestation.

order.why: Consider recognition beyond scholarly rank and inherited precautions.
shortened: And regarding infallibility, the Primal Point, exalted and glorified be He, hath declared that whosoever believeth in Him is infallible, and whosoever believeth not is bereft of infallibility. He hath further declared that infallibility is not what the followers of the Qur'an have imagined, who have regarded religious precautions as infallibility. Rather, infallibility belongeth to him who, at the time of the Manifestation, believeth in God, even though he be accounted among the lowliest of creation.

order.why: Read protection through speaking what the revealed Word has spoken.
Preserve the Báb’s charge to receive and forgo.
shortened: O believers, whatsoever fruit of the Messenger He giveth you, accept it, and whatsoever He forbiddeth you, forgo it, for God hath made him wise in truth before Us.

order.why: Keep the historically situated discussion of signs and lineage.
shortened: Otherwise we must regard as admissible the opening of the Gate of Saintship, and consider that He Who is to arise of the family of Muhammad possesses two signs: the first condition, Holy Lineage; the second, [that He is divinely] fortified with brilliant verses.

order.why: Hear the appeal to turn toward the divine summons.
Make steadfastness a subject of prayer for protection.
Clarify received protection through the moon’s borrowed light.
shortened: As to infallibility, it is possible for man to be under divine protection and God may preserve him from error. For instance, the moon has no light of itself but receives light from the sun. This is the infallibility of the human world. A skilled physician protects man from every illness. Praise be to God that you are serving through divine teachings, and the more you serve, the more doubts will vanish and the manifest truth will become clear and evident.

order.why: Read the prayer for guidance and its stated requirements.
shortened: O Thou Kind One, grant them a refuge and shelter and bestow upon them a protecting sanctuary, that they may abide under the shadow of Thy protection and care and be preserved from error. For the great sinner cannot be the manifest guardian, and the erring invalid cannot be the protector of the mighty Faith, and the misguided one cannot be the guide to the path, and one liable to error cannot be the center of guidance and the expounder of the mighty verses.

order.why: Connect protection of the Centre of the Covenant with unity.
shortened: The purpose of the Blessed Beauty in entering into this Covenant and Testament was to gather all existent beings around one point so that the thoughtless souls, who in every cycle and generation have been the cause of dissension, may not undermine the Cause. He hath, therefore, commanded that whatever emanateth from the Centre of the Covenant is right and is under His protection and favour, while all else is error.

order.why: Retain the reported account of the Covenant’s provision.
Read the reported distinction beside the fuller authoritative explanation.
shortened: Infallibility is of two kinds; 1) Intrinsic or immediate Infallibility, 2) conferred, extrinsic or mediate Infallibility. Intrinsic or immediate Infallibility means that of God, exalted is His Glory, and none else save Him has any portion thereof.

The conferred, extrinsic or mediate Infallibility is that of those Holy Souls who are under the protection of the Divine Manifestations, for preservation from error is conferred upon souls as a pure gift of God. God's Infallibility is intrinsic, whereas that of the Holy Souls under the protection of His Manifestations is extrinsic, for it is acquired as a gift or quality from them. For instance, the light of the Sun is intrinsic or immediate, but the light of the planets is acquired from the Sun and is therefore extrinsic. The light of the Sun is independent of the planet, while that of the planet is dependent upon the light of the Sun.

order.why: Keep the reported identification of the Universal House of Justice.
Retain the further report on its protection.
Close linked selections with a reported criticism whose historical claim needs contextual reading.
Begin supplied readings with the stated bond between revelation and infallibility.
Examine the supplied discussion of investigative method.
shortened: To the Baha'is, therefore, the Revealed Word is the balance, the infallible balance, by which truth can be distinguished from error. The human mind is too limited, too impotent to be able, all alone, to understand the purpose and plan of God for His creation. The source of ultimate guidance, therefore, is the Prophet. His word is infallible. If it seems to be in conflict with prevailing notions and standards, this is no sufficient reason to justify us to repudiate it. Rather we should endeavor to so direct our methods of investigation as to be able to reach the very same conclusions the Prophet has arrived at.

order.why: Keep its explicit affirmation of continued personal investigation.
Remember the limits placed upon ordinary human perfection.
Read the supplied account of prophetic preservation.
Explore the supplied Shaykhi definition and the accompanying terminology.
shortened: "As for how the `Adliyya define `isma, their definition is the most appropriate. The gist of the correct part of their definition is that (`isma) is a divine disposition that prevents the act of disobeying and intending to do so while retaining the capability to do it.... The ma`sum abstains from all the things that God has prohibited."
In the Baha'i writings, `isma is translated as "infallibility," "sinlessness," and "protection."

order.why: Return to consultation in the supplied selection.
Consider the protection attributed to explicit written provisions.
Distinguish the institutions named from personal opinionatedness.
End with the supplied account of the emergence of administration.
shortened: Out of the pangs of anguish which His bereaved followers have suffered, amid the heat and dust which the attacks launched by a sleepless enemy had precipitated, the Administration of Baha'u'llah's invincible Faith was born. The potent energies released through the ascension of the Center of His Covenant crystallized into this supreme, this infallible Organ for the accomplishment of a Divine Purpose. The Will and Testament of 'Abdu'l-Baha unveiled its character, reaffirmed its basis, supplemented its principles, asserted its indispensability, and enumerated its chief institutions.

questions: Which different meanings of infallibility are distinguished here, and what becomes confused when they are treated as identical?
How does the sun-and-reflection analogy clarify the relationship between essential and conferred protection?
What do the discussions of prophetic penitence and scriptural reproach suggest about interpretation?
What does Hebrews illuminate about sinlessness and compassion, and which institutional questions remain specific to this compilation?
How do the supplied passages describe continued investigation within commitment to revelation?
What further questions about scope, membership, consultation, and authority would you take to the connected House of Justice compilation?

references.label: 1 · Hebrews 4:14–16 · Sinlessness and compassionate understanding
references.note: Hebrews presents Jesus as the high priest who understands human weakness and has faced temptation without sin, then invites the community to approach for mercy and help. Compare this conjunction of perfection and compassionate guidance with the compilation’s discussions of prophetic sinlessness. The Christian passage concerns Christ’s priestly role; it does not itself offer the Bahá’í distinction between essential and conferred infallibility or define institutional authority.

subjects.displayTitle: Obligatory prayer: the daily return to a beloved presence
subjects.introduction: For a lover there is no greater pleasure than conversing with the beloved, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes, and that is the wisdom of obligatory prayer: at a fixed hour each day a person turns with heart and soul toward God, and every grief, He says, dissolves the moment He begins. Bahá’u’lláh asks the one who prays to stand severed from all things and to ask that the prayer become a fire burning away the veils and a light leading to the ocean of His presence. Outward forms carry an inward attention, and together with fasting such prayer is the moon and sun of religion. The practice has a history, from the ordinances of the Báb and an earlier prayer of nine rak‘ahs to the three prayers that replaced it, any of which may be chosen, as the official note explains [2]. When God called Moses He joined His oneness to establishing prayer for remembrance [1]. The way continues toward the law of fasting, the power of prayer, and the state in which prayer becomes an encounter rather than a repetition.
subjects.arc: Begin with communion and joy, encounter the later prayers, then read their discipline and historical development in context.

order.why: Open with prayer understood as loving companionship.
shortened: The wisdom of obligatory prayer is this: That it causeth a connection between the servant and the True One, because at that time man with all his heart and soul turneth his face towards the Almighty, seeking His association and desiring His love and companionship. For a lover, there is no greater pleasure than to converse with his beloved, and for a seeker, there is no greater bounty than intimacy with the object of his desire. It is the greatest longing of every soul who is attracted to the Kingdom of God to find time to turn with entire devotion to his Beloved, so as to seek His bounty and blessing and immerse himself in the ocean of communion, entreaty and supplication.

order.why: Let the lived experience of joy give the practice warmth.
Read the complete short prayer’s acknowledgment of purpose and need.
Enter the long prayer through its opening request for fire and light.
shortened: Whoso wisheth to recite this prayer, let him stand up and turn unto God, and, as he standeth in his place, let him gaze to the right and to the left, as if awaiting the mercy of his Lord, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Then let him say:

O Thou Who art the Lord of all names and the Maker of the heavens! I beseech Thee by them Who are the Day-Springs of Thine invisible Essence, the Most Exalted, the All-Glorious, to make of my prayer a fire that will burn away the veils which have shut me out from Thy beauty, and a light that will lead me unto the ocean of Thy Presence.

order.why: Hear the medium prayer begin with preparation of the hands.
shortened: Whoso wisheth to pray, let him wash his hands, and while he washeth, let him say:

Strengthen my hand, O my God, that it may take hold of Thy Book with such steadfastness that the hosts of the world shall have no power over it. Guard it, then, from meddling with whatsoever doth not belong unto it. Thou art, verily, the Almighty, the Most Powerful.
Medium obligatory prayer, to be recited daily, in the morning, at noon, and in the evening.

order.why: Connect the obligation with humility and nearness.
Read the pleasure of intimate conversation.
shortened: There is a pleasure in offering prayers that transcends all other pleasures, and there is a sweetness in chanting and singing the verses of God which is the greatest desire of all the believers, men and women alike. While reciting the Obligatory Prayer, one converses intimately and shares secrets with the true Beloved. No pleasure is greater than this, if one proceeds with a detached soul, with tears overflowing, with a trusting heart and an eager spirit. Every joy is earthly save this one, the sweetness of which is divine.

order.why: Consider the inward condition of genuine prayer.
shortened: O My brother! How great, how very great, can the law of obligatory prayer be, when, through His mercy and loving kindness, one is enabled to observe it. When a man commenceth the recitation of the Obligatory Prayer, he should see himself severed from all created things and regard himself as utter nothingness before the will and purpose of God, in such wise that he seeth naught but Him in the world of being. This is the station of God’s well-favored ones and those who are wholly devoted to Him.

order.why: Follow devotion toward renewed life.
Introduce prayer as a ladder beside fasting’s light.
State nearness as the purpose of both ordinances.
Read the sun-and-moon image of the two pillars.
Keep the related prayerful appeal in its own source.
Connect hope with outward practice.
shortened: For the station of hope is manifested through outward deeds, and fasting and prayer are as the sun and moon in the heaven of divine ordinances. Seize upon these twain through the power of thy Lord, O thou who soarest in the atmosphere of the love of God!

order.why: Let remembrance and awareness of poverty join the discipline.
Place prayer within the continuity and changing forms of revelation.
shortened: The traditions established the fact that in all Dispensations the law of prayer hath constituted a fundamental element of the Revelation of all the Prophets of God -- a law the form and the manner of which hath been adapted to the varying requirements of every age.

order.why: Read the earlier Aqdas provision and its accompanying ordinances.
shortened: We have enjoined obligatory prayer upon you, with nine rak'ahs, to be offered at noon and in the morning and the evening unto God, the Revealer of Verses. We have relieved you of a greater number, as a command in the Book of God.

We have commanded you to pray and fast from the beginning of maturity; this is ordained by God, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers. He hath exempted from this those who are weak from illness or age, as a bounty from His Presence, and He is the Forgiving, the Generous.
Perform ye, likewise, ablutions for the Obligatory Prayer; this is the command of God, the Incomparable, the Unrestrained.

order.why: Identify the three later prayers as accepted alternatives.
shortened: Regarding the prayer with nine-rak'ats about which you inquired - that prayer, along with some writings from the Sacred Texts, has fallen into the hands of the Covenant-breakers.
As to the other three obligatory prayers, these likewise are valid alternatives: whichever of them be practised shall be accepted. And the prayer before sunrise is permissible.

order.why: Keep the explicit reference to choosing one of the three.
shortened: The Obligatory Prayers have been set down by the Pen of the Most High and have been mentioned in the Persian "Questions and Answers", which supplementeth the Kitab-i-Aqdas. They are clearly binding, and without a doubt everyone must perform one of these three prayers....

order.why: Read the earlier withholding of a prayer in its historical setting.
Preserve the Báb’s distinct nineteen-rak’ah ordinance.
Read its particular instructions for ablutions in their own dispensation.
Keep the Báb’s treatment of prayer and ritual water.
shortened: Know that prayer is the first fruit of religion and upon it revolve all deeds. It is the first thing God made obligatory upon His servants. In its entirety within God's Book, it is the temple of unity springing from the heart. None shall be accepted who does not know its laws, and none shall be elevated save through observing all its stations.

order.why: Attend to the distinction concerning the call and standing prayer.
Read the selected ablution prayer in its earlier scriptural setting.
shortened: And if thou desirest to attain the summit of grace and reach the Most Exalted Habitation, and have ordained for thee every good thing in the heaven of destiny from thy Lord, the Most High, the Most Glorious, then detach thyself from all things, then perform ablutions with pure, clean water as thou wert commanded in the Bayan from an ancient Revealer, and when thou washest thy hands say: "O my Lord! Purify me from all else save Thee, then make me ready to meet Thee in the Day of the manifestation of Thy Beauty and the appearance of Thy Self, then sanctify me from that which hath veiled me from Thy resplendent Beauty, and deliver me, O my God, for the recognition of Thy exalted, all-knowing Self."

order.why: Notice the allowance against unnecessary renewal of ablutions.
Retain the selected question about previously performed ablutions.
Distinguish individual prayer from synchronized recitation.
shortened: As to the obligatory prayer (to be said three times a day): Each one must say his prayer alone by himself, and this is not conditional on a private place; that is, both at home and in the worshipping-place, which is a gathering-place, it is allowable for one to say his prayer; but each person must say his prayer by himself (i. e., not in company with others who might recite the same words and continue the same postures together at the same time).

order.why: Read the reported explanation of personal obligatory worship.
Introduce the fixed direction of prayer.
shortened: Orientation is spiritual connection and attachment, and seeking guidance is a divine matter of the heart through divine inspiration, and the remembrance of thy Gracious Lord is through spiritual attraction sanctified from directions, for all directions are His directions. As to the Obligatory Prayer, it hath a Qiblih that is fixed, specified, holy and blessed.

order.why: Read the text identifying its scriptural basis.
Keep an earlier regional instruction within its time and circumstances.
Preserve the related statement that an announcement was still to come.
Read the selected clarification concerning the noon prayer.
Keep the reported scheduling account distinct from the prayers’ own directions.
Retain the further reported instruction with its source status visible.
Read the reported description of alternatives in context.
Hear the personal encouragement to use the long prayer.
Clarifies the relation of the long obligatory prayer to the other two forms.
Distinguish a prayerful attitude from particular prescribed prayers.
Clarify the relation between obligatory and additional supplications.
Read their conjunction in the source’s language.
Connect sustained prayer with firmness and gladness.
Give regularity and mindfulness their place.
shortened: Be constant in prayer and mindful in fasting. Day and night occupy yourselves with devotion, supplication and prayer, especially at the designated time.

order.why: Hear the appeal to guide others toward prayer.
shortened: You must certainly guide everyone to perform their prayers, for it is the ascension of spirits and the lamp of the hearts of the righteous. It is the living waters of the paradise of good-pleasure and an explicitly ordained duty from the All-Merciful. Delay and negligence are never permissible.

order.why: Retain the direct assertion of obligation.
Read the severe warning without detaching it from the law’s exemptions.
Connect worship and community building.
Keep the brief reminder that worship is commanded in the Book.
Read adherence to ordinances as part of steadfastness.
Return to the Most Holy Book as the point of reference.
shortened: Today all must fix their gaze upon the divine ordinances and act in accordance with whatsoever hath been revealed in the Most Holy Book.

order.why: Let law appear as lamp and living water.
shortened: The divine laws are a luminous lamp amidst the servants and living waters for those who have turned unto them and act upon them.

order.why: Keep the testimony of practice amid hardship.
shortened: This Wronged One and those who accept Him in this land hold fast to the strong cord of fasting and prayer and the deeds mentioned in the Book.

order.why: Connect worship with firmly rooted belief.
shortened: In whatever land you enter, guide all to firmness and steadfastness in God's Covenant, and likewise to adherence to the contents of the treatise written in response to Aqa Mirza Abu'l-Fadl, upon him be the Glory of God, and most importantly to the implementation of divine worship ordinances such as prayer and fasting with utmost strength. Since the contents of the treatise relate to established true beliefs, therefore they must first become firmly rooted in the heart, then one should engage in worship.

order.why: Distinguish required devotion from elaborate austerities.
shortened: We who practiced no austerities, observed no continual fasts, performed no elaborate worship, and offered no lengthy prayers - at most we carried out the obligatory devotions and divine ordinances - despite this deficiency, the grace and favor of the King of Manifestation so encompassed us that we found the path of guidance and gained shelter beneath the blessed tree.

order.why: Retain the historical report concerning gradual practicability.
Close linked readings with steadfast service and life according to the Book.
shortened: O thou who hast turned thy face toward the Kingdom of God! I supplicate God that thou mayest become like unto Peter, the "Rock"--unshaken, immovable and strong; be assisted by heavenly confirmation; be helped to the service of the Cause of God, opening thy tongue to teach the divine instructions, and living and walking according to the laws of the Book of Aqdas.

order.why: Read the supplied exhortation through its images of ascent and life.
End with the supplied invitation to discover the prayers through regular use.

questions: How do the images of companionship, light, water, and ascent change your understanding of an obligation?
What relationship do the passages describe between outward preparation and inward attention?
How might regular practice nourish joy without reducing prayer to repetition?
What does the Qur’anic connection between prayer and remembrance illuminate about this collection?
How does distinguishing earlier provisions, later prayers, and reported accounts improve your reading of the practical instructions?
What could the connected subjects of fasting and the state of prayer add to the relationship between devotion and daily conduct?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 20:14 · Prayer and remembrance
references.note: In the Qur’anic account of Moses’ calling, God joins the declaration of divine oneness with worship and the establishment of prayer for remembrance. Read this verse in Mustafa Khattab’s translation beside the compilation’s accounts of turning toward the Beloved. The connection concerns prayer’s spiritual orientation; the specific forms and schedules of the two religious traditions require their own texts.

references.label: 2 · The Kitáb-i-Aqdas, note 3 · Historical clarification
references.note: The official note explains that the earlier obligatory prayer was superseded by three prayers later revealed by Bahá’u’lláh, and that an individual may choose any one of those three. Its cross-references lead to their texts and practical instructions. Use this clarification when reading the compilation’s earlier provisions and differing reported descriptions; those historical selections have been preserved rather than silently rewritten.

subjects.displayTitle: Spiritual knowledge: what learning becomes in a human life
subjects.introduction: Knowledge, Bahá’u’lláh says, is of two kinds, and the difference lies in its spring and its fruit. One wells up from divine inspiration and bears patience, longing, understanding and love; the other reflects vain thoughts driven by selfish desire, and yields only arrogance and conceit. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá therefore insists that character must come first, since learning joined to bad conduct is a deadly poison, while learning conjoined with the love of God is a blessed tree. None of this is a retreat from science; the friends are urged to make schoolchildren the most erudite of the wise. But understanding the words of God depends on purity of heart, and the ear that hears the divine call is not the piece of flesh on the side of the head. James drew the same line between a wisdom marked by envy and strife and one that is gentle, merciful and full of good fruits [1]. From here the inquiry turns to the four methods of acquiring knowledge, to the inmost heart that perceives, and to inspiration and its discernment.
subjects.arc: Begin with the ethical fruits of knowledge, join learning to spiritual receptivity, and test illumination through humility and service.

order.why: Open with the moral conditions that make knowledge beneficial.
shortened: Good behaviour and high moral character must come first, for unless the character be trained, acquiring knowledge will only prove injurious. Knowledge is praiseworthy when it is coupled with ethical conduct and virtuous character; otherwise it is a deadly poison, a frightful danger.

order.why: Distinguish kinds of knowledge through their origins and fruits.
shortened: Know verily that Knowledge is of two kinds: Divine and Satanic. The one welleth out from the fountain of divine inspiration; the other is but a reflection of vain and obscure thoughts. The source of the former is God Himself; the motive-force of the latter the whisperings of selfish desire.
The former bringeth forth the fruit of patience, of longing desire, of true understanding, and love; whilst the latter can yield naught but arrogance, vainglory and conceit.

order.why: Welcome whatever increases genuine vision.
Affirm vigorous pursuit of learning, culture and science.
Give children’s education a concrete social purpose.
Connect eager study with the advancement of a people.
Join scientific accomplishment with refined character.
shortened: Whereas the development of good character and refinement of morals is more important than the acquisition of sciences.

The acquisition of sciences and arts, after faith and certitude, is among the greatest virtues of the human world, but on condition that the pursuit of knowledge be coupled with refinement of character and inspiration from the light of divine effulgence.

order.why: Read the consequences of learning without moral growth.
Keep sciences and crafts beside the need for spiritual education.
shortened: Thereafter, efforts must be made to teach them sciences, crafts and knowledge to the extent possible, for without heavenly virtues and upright character, the mere acquisition of learning and arts will not suffice and will not prevent moral corruption and the harms of self and passion, but rather will become the cause of promoting false thoughts and a means of strengthening personal interests, unless accompanied by divine education.

order.why: Read the reported contrast between worldly learning and lived spiritual teaching.
shortened: No fruits whatsoever will be manifested from those who are educated in the worldly things and remain unaware of spiritual matters. However, those among the believers who live in accordance with the divine teachings, ordinances and exhortations, shall be confirmed.

order.why: Consider physical, intellectual and spiritual requirements together.
shortened: Herein we learn that man is a representative of the physical, intellectual and spiritual world. Just as in his physical environment he is in need of material things; in his spiritual environment he requires celestial things. Just as the amelioration and perfection of the world of humanity is dependent upon the progress of sciences and art, so also the refinement of the spirit and the cultivation of the highest ideals of morality is made possib[le] through celestial sciences and art.

order.why: Read the tree of knowledge through the fruit it bears.
shortened: And every branch of learning, conjoined with the love of God, is approved and worthy of praise; but bereft of His love, learning is barren -- indeed, it bringeth on madness. Every kind of knowledge, every science, is as a tree: if the fruit of it be the love of God, then is it a blessed tree, but if not, that tree is but dried-up wood, and shall only feed the fire.

order.why: Explore the relation between a learner’s river and the sea.
shortened: Although to acquire the sciences and arts is the greatest glory of mankind, this is so only on condition that manis river flow into the mighty sea, and draw from Godis ancient source His inspiration. When this cometh to pass, then every teacher is as a shoreless ocean, every pupil a prodigal fountain of knowledge. If, then, the pursuit of knowledge lead to the beauty of Him Who is the Object of all Knowledge, how excellent that goal; but if not, a mere drop will perhaps shut a man off from flooding grace, for with learning cometh arrogance and pride, and it bringeth on error and indifference to God.

order.why: Let knowledge and faith become complementary wings.
Connect the movement of the heart with knowledge and physical capacities.
shortened: And since the heart has become weak from the absence of spiritual power, it can no longer observe divine mysteries and its future affairs.
So if you want to have lofty aspirations, you must set the heart in motion to unite with knowledge - that is, to join spiritual virtues with physical perfections.

order.why: Connects divine knowledge with independent perception, purification and detachment.
Read wisdom and recognition in relation to public well-being.
shortened: A true philosopher would never deny God nor His evidences, rather would he acknowledge His glory and overpowering majesty which overshadow all created things.

Say: The beginning of Wisdom and the origin thereof is to acknowledge whatsoever God hath clearly set forth, for through its potency the foundation of statesmanship, which is a shield for the preservation of the body of mankind, hath been firmly established.

order.why: Trace the Tree of Wisdom to knowledge of God.
Distinguish a source of knowledge from unsupported claims.
shortened: Hold fast to the Source of knowledge and its Mine, that thou mayest find thyself independent of all who claim knowledge without clear evidence or an illuminating Book.

order.why: Hear the definition of the truly learned in the cited revelation.
Connect learning with action according to the Book.
Read maturity through the restraint and direction of knowledge.
shortened: The truly learned one is he whose knowledge prevents him from all that My good-pleasure and His good-pleasure abhorreth, and the mature one is he who hath attained unto the dawning-place of My knowledge; and apart from this none is mature, even though he may live for [many] years.

order.why: Consider the removal of imaginings as preparation for certitude.
Introduce the inner eye and ear.
shortened: Open thine inner eye that thou mayest behold the face of the Beloved, and hearken with thine inner ear that thou mayest hear the sweet murmur of His celestial voice.

order.why: Read sensory language as a call to spiritual perception.
shortened: O servants! Sight belongeth to the eye and hearing to the ear. Whoso in this blessed day hath not heard the voice of the divine herald hath not possessed, nor doth he possess, ears. The ear is not that piece of flesh at which thou gazest - open the hidden eye that thou mayest behold the fire of God, and hearken with the ear of the spirit that thou mayest hear the sweet voice of the Beloved.

order.why: Keep the reported sensory analogy within its spiritual argument.
shortened: A blind man, though he sit near the light, cannot see it; but a clear-sighted man can see from afar. A man afflicted with a cold, if he be in a rose garden, cannot inhale the fragrances, but one whose nostrils are pure can inhale from a long distance. The people who are in these cities are deaf and blind, but you, having an open eye and a pure nostril, can see the Light from afar and inhale the fragrances of this Rose Garden.

order.why: Distinguish immediate awareness from arguments addressed to another.
shortened: These are theoretical arguments adduced for weak souls, but if the eye of inner vision be opened, a hundred thousand clear proofs will be seen. Thus, when man feels the indwelling spirit, he is in no need of arguments for its existence; but for those who are deprived of the grace of the spirit, it is necessary to set forth external arguments.

order.why: Read the appeal to insight beside the neighboring inquiry into methods.
Consider thirst and capacity before the reception of living water.
Keep the claim concerning the Holy Spirit and highest truth.
Read gathered water and rain as differing images of wisdom.
shortened: Earthly wisdom is as the water of pools, gathered from this side and from that, while Heavenly Wisdom is as rain. Earthly wisdom is as the light of a lamp, while Heavenly Wisdom is as the ever-shining radiance of the stars. If the Heavenly Wisdom should pass away from this world, all human beings would perish.

order.why: Introduce the continuously flowing fountain of knowledge.
shortened: The divine outpourings are never cut off - at all times the Kawthar of knowledge of the All-Merciful flows and spreads forth from the fountainhead of will, and its bestower is the hands of grace of the Lord.

order.why: Turn receptivity into a request for enduring illumination.
Follow the transformation of drop and atom through guidance.
shortened: O thou who hast attained to the recognition of the All-Merciful!

Today, attainment unto the Most Great Guidance is among the supreme gifts of the All-Glorious Lord and is the most noble magnet attracting the outpourings of the realms above and the Abha Kingdom. For the divine lights are shining with intense brilliance and mighty radiance from the horizons of human consciousness. Through His grace, the drop findeth the station of the sea, and through the bounty of the Truth, the atom becometh the brilliant sun of guidance.

order.why: Consider the responsibility to guard the pearl of recognition.
shortened: Say: O ye who drink the choice wine of utterance, know ye your worth and preserve your stations, and guard the unique pearl, which is the knowledge of God, exalted be His glory, as a treasure within the repository of the heart from thieves and traitors.

order.why: Connect hearing at Sinai with the present divine call.
Read revelation as an enduring table of nourishment.
shortened: The tables mentioned in the Bible are spiritual tables. The effect of the material table lasts for twelve hours but that which is divine is everlasting and eternal.
For example,--'Revelation' is one of the heavenly tables. As an illustration, think of the knowledge revealed two thousand years ago; we feel the effect of it now and that effect will remain forever.

order.why: Attend to the many forms of spiritual food.
Keep the reported table conversation in its own setting.
Distinguish an enduring treasure from passing gain.
shortened: But, praised be the Lord, thou art engaged in that which secureth for thee a gain that shall eternally endure; and that is naught but thine attraction to the Kingdom of God, thy faith, and thy knowledge, the enlightenment of thine heart, and thine earnest endeavour to promote the Divine Teachings.
Verily this gift is imperishable and this wealth is a treasure from on high!

order.why: Read faith and recognition as a form of wealth.
Retain the reported counsel concerning children’s learning.
shortened: You have to make them learn by heart some of these verses. By these means they will become enlightened and well educated, for they are like unto a young tree: you can train them in whatever manner you like.

order.why: Examine the reported example of virtue without formal schooling.
Read the particular account of writing attributed to spiritual attachment.
shortened: "This is also one of the most distinctive signs of the Baha'i cycle that a person who has never entered the doors of a school, who has not studied grammar and syntax sitsdown and writes such scholarly works; for example a man like Mirza Mohamad Afshar who has written such a significant book. To those who are just, there is no greater proof than this! This is purely through the gift of the Lord! Because their hearts are so attached to the Cause, that that very attachment becomes an unerring teacher. Their words have life...

order.why: Keep the reported encouragement to a sincere worker in its context.
shortened: In the Spiritual Station you will never be without the Knowledge necessary to answer a question.

order.why: Balance confidence with awareness of mistakes and shortcomings.
Judge spiritual claims through daily thoughts, speech and deeds.
shortened: Therefore let not any considerations of physical relationship hinder you from recognizing the truth. In this Dispensation none of these matters have the weight of a mustard seed. Every person, no matter who he is - must be judged according to the standard of spirituality, sanctity, severance, attraction, fidelity to and service in the Cause - which he manifests in his daily thoughts, speeches and deeds. This is the unerring criterion and the searching test ...

order.why: Connect moral refinement with the foundations of civilization.
shortened: The foundation of civilization is the amelioration of the conditions of morality; the basis of spirituality is the purity of morality. The Everlasting Glory of the world of humanity is in the readjustment of morality. The power and the potency of man is through the refinement of morality. And the beautification and refinement of morality is impossible except through the Breathes of the Holy-Spirit.

order.why: Read divine civilization as a horizon for human maturation.
Keep the spiritual character of the movement explicit.
shortened: It is not a political movement, it is not an industrial movement, it is not a scientific movement, -- but it is the influence of the Word of God, it is the breath of the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Distinguish illumination of humanity from temporal dominion.
Read the call to spiritual matters within its counsel concerning political conflict.
Retain the motivation toward light without omitting responsibility in the source context.
Join a foundation in existence with an aspiration toward eternity.
Locate wisdom in the heart rather than material constitution.
shortened: Thus it becomes clear and evident that manliness and wisdom belong to the heart, not to water and clay. This being so, strive to become a man of the arena of divine knowledge and a luminous star in the heaven.

order.why: Invite sustained inquiry into meanings and realities.
Read spiritual powers in mutual assistance.
Let renewed light answer weariness and confusion.
shortened: This languor and listlessness is like a cloud - the Sun of Reality will eventually disperse it through the heat of its rays, and darkness and error will pass away and the dawn of guidance will break forth.

order.why: Consider harmony as the quality prized in illumination.
Close linked readings with words and meanings bringing life together.
Read the supplied statement of knowledge through the Manifestation.
End with the supplied poetic contrast inviting further reflection.

questions: What signs distinguish knowledge that enlarges understanding from knowledge that feeds conceit?
How do the passages connect scientific and artistic learning with character and spiritual purpose?
What do images of food, water, sight, and a fruitful tree contribute to the meaning of knowing?
How does James’ account of wisdom’s fruits help you examine claims to spiritual insight?
How might confidence in divine assistance coexist with awareness of personal mistakes?
What questions would you take to the connected subjects of inspiration and methods of knowing about the relationship between conviction and discernment?

references.label: 1 · James 3:13–18 · Wisdom recognized by its fruits
references.note: James contrasts wisdom associated with envy and strife with wisdom expressed through gentleness, mercy, good fruits, and peace. The comparison is especially close to the compilation’s distinction between knowledge that nurtures understanding and knowledge that produces pride. Both direct attention to the knower’s conduct; the Bahá’í passages also develop their own account of recognition of revelation and the spiritual foundations of education.

subjects.displayTitle: Visitation: remembrance as a meeting of hearts
subjects.introduction: Standing at a grave, we find that memory wants to speak in the second person: peace be upon you, light upon your dust. The Visitation Tablets give that instinct a sacred form, addressing the Báb, Imam Husayn, martyrs and particular believers by name, bearing witness to their virtues, and asking mercy both for the one remembered and for whoever remembers. The approach itself matters: turning the face toward the resting place, pausing in stillness, declaring the unity of God at the sanctuary gate. Yet presence is not only bodily. When the road is barred the heart may turn instead, and friends may recite on another’s behalf, weeping together over a distant grave. A narration in Sahih Muslim preserves a simple greeting for the graveyard that joins address, shared mortality and prayer, and sets off by contrast the richness of these particular commemorations [1]. The journey continues through eulogies that keep a life’s qualities alive, through reminiscences of those who served, and through the wider world of prayer, until remembrance returns the visitor to daily life with renewed fidelity and the will to serve.
subjects.arc: Begin with remembrance across distance, approach the place of visitation, and follow individual salutations toward shared memory and renewed service.

order.why: Read collective recitation and circulation of the prayer.
shortened: O Hands of the Cause of God! This visitation prayer should be recited by me along with a group of the loved ones of God at the fragrant resting place of that promulgator of God's Cause on a special day, and you should disseminate this visitation prayer among all the loved ones.

order.why: Open with the heart’s turning when a physical journey is barred.
Connect remembrance with renewed spiritual powers.
shortened: Happy is thy condition, for thou art enjoying Eternal Life in the Kingdom of Everlasting Glory and hast left in this world kind and loving Remembrances. Happy are those souls who visit thy luminous resting-place and through thy commemoration receive and acquire spiritual Powers.

order.why: Hear the visitor’s own prayer for forgiveness.
shortened: Glory be unto Thee, O God, Lord of the world and Master of nations! I beseech Thee by the Most Great Name through which Thy path was established and Thy balance was set up, and through which the ocean of grandeur surged and the mountains passed away, to forgive me and my father and whosoever hath believed in Thee and Thy signs. O my Lord! Thou seest me standing before the tomb of Thy friend and chosen one.

order.why: Join blessing of the departed with blessing of those who remember.
shortened: Radiant glory and effulgent splendour be upon all who seek out thy resting-place, who visit thee, and call thee to remembrance for the sake of God, the Lord of all worlds; and upon thee, upon thy beginning and thy end, upon thy outer and thy inner being, rest His light and mercy, his grace, his loving favours, his providence and blessings.

order.why: Attend to orientation, stillness and magnification before visitation.
Read the Báb’s preparation through purity, rest and silent approach.
shortened: And when thou desirest to enter that sacred land, purify thyself and make wholesome what is with thee to the best of thy ability. Know thou that there is the most exalted horizon of the Throne and the ultimate summit of Paradise, and that God doth ever behold thee, and the Manifestations of His Self do ever illumine thee.

When thou hast performed such ablutions as thou art able, lie down for a while until thy strength returneth unto thee. Then arise and pray two rak'ahs in thy house, then walk in silence until thou reachest the first gate.

order.why: Keep the declaration of divine unity at the sanctuary gate.
shortened: Know, O my brother, that the law of visitation is thus: When thou standest at the gate of the sanctuary, say: I bear witness that there is no God but God, alone without partner, One God, Single, Unique, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Eternal, Who hath ever been, and before Whose existence nothing was, and Who shall ever be as He hath been, without mention of aught else.

order.why: Preserve the particular shrine instructions in their own setting.
shortened: When you enter the Blessed Shrine, pray in the small chamber near the abandoned well, then turn towards the Kaaba and say: I bear witness that there is no God but God, alone, with no partner, just as His Essence has testified to His Essence that there is no God but He, the Mighty, the Wise.

order.why: Read the request for words concerning visitation.
Introduce the Báb’s prayer for faithful respondents and martyrs.
shortened: This is a prayer and visitation for the first to respond to his Lord, for the manifestations of His Self, and for the martyrs in His path.

order.why: Hear the salutation and its question of adequate description.
shortened: Then say: "Peace be upon thee, O Abu-'Abdu'llah, and the mercy of God and His blessings. How can I describe thee, O my Master, when I am certain that all paths of existence are blocked before thee, and all attributes of things in thy presence return unto themselves?

order.why: Identify the visitation for Husayn in its stated context.
shortened: This is a Visitation Tablet revealed by My Most Glorious Pen in the Most Exalted Horizon for His Holiness the Prince of Martyrs, Husayn ibn 'Ali - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for him.

order.why: Read the Báb’s symbolic account without manufacturing an interpretation.
shortened: He it is Who accepteth from his visitor through the true visitation of Himself, and Who hath called unto his place of martyrdom in truth by His throne -- there is no God but He -- without similitude in truth, and God hath not ordained for his mystery any interpretation upon a single letter. He it is Who hath promised His visitor the meeting with Himself, and God's promise was in truth, upon truth, fulfilled. He it is Who hath ordained the fourfold in the fourfold from the paths of visitation in the visitation, in truth upon truth, and the matter in the Mother Book was decreed around the Fire.

order.why: Let the repeated salutations disclose the language of reverence.
shortened: Then say: Peace be upon Thee, O Essence of Eternity in the exaltation of Glory! Peace be upon Thee, O Camphor of Pre-existence in the ascendancy of Beauty! Peace be upon Thee, O Pure Essence of Bounty in the immunity of Perfection! Peace be upon Thee, O Essence of Mystery in the exaltation of Most Holy Action! Peace be upon Thee, O Pure Embodiment of Command at the ultimate pinnacle of might and justice!

order.why: Keep the named address and request for permission distinct.
Retain the title and praise of this particular visitation.
Read the Tablet for Hasan with its own stated relationship.
shortened: This is the Tablet of Visitation which hath been sent down from the Kingdom of Eternity for the Name of God Who was called Hasan and was related to His Self, the All-Compelling, the Mighty, the Self-Subsisting. Blessed are they who visit him and are among the visitors and draw nigh through him unto God, the Mighty, the Beloved.

order.why: Attend to the testimony concerning the first response to the Call.
Keep the particular salutation to Vahid.
shortened: The first wave of exaltation from the ocean of grace of thy Lord, the Compassionate, be upon thee [Vahid] who art the essence of the Qur'an and possessor of the mysteries of the Bayan.

order.why: Read remembered sacrifice through the enduring written word.
shortened: We have immortalized thy mention by My Most Exalted Pen in the Crimson Scroll which none but God, the Creator of all things, hath beheld, and We have remembered thee in this Tablet with that which shall cause those near unto God to remember thee and cause the sincere ones to turn toward thy resting-place.
Blessed art thou, and felicity be unto thee and unto him who presenteth himself before thy grave and reciteth that which the All-Bountiful hath revealed concerning the final end.

order.why: Give the martyred handmaiden a place in the lament.
shortened: Whoever wishes to visit the handmaiden who was martyred, let them recite this Visitation Prayer:
In the Name of God, the Most Exalted, the Most High

O Supreme Pen! Joy did not overtake thee in the days of thy Lord, the Most High, that thou mightest warble upon the branches of the Divine Lote-Tree with the melodies of Baha. Rather, thou wert touched by the supreme calamity whereupon the earth and heaven wailed.

order.why: Hear the direct visit to a handmaiden’s resting place.
Preserve the jointly named martyrs in their particular Tablet.
shortened: This is a visitation prayer revealed by God, the Lord of Names, for His loved ones (Jinab-i-Ashraf, Basir and Mirza Muhammad-'Ali) who turned to the place of detachment for martyrdom and were martyred in the path of God in the land of Za.

order.why: Read the renewed tale of sacrifice at Husayn’s grave.
shortened: Blessed is he who visits My Name Husayn, concerning whom My Most Exalted Pen has spoken, and who says before his grave:
"By God! Through you the tale of sacrifice was renewed, and the Concourse on High lamented, and the Lote-Tree of the Far Boundary cried out.

order.why: Keep the identification of the prayer for Mirza Ali-Muhammad.
shortened: That which hath been revealed in the visitation (prayer) for Mirza ‘Ali-Muhammad, who was martyred in the path of God.

order.why: Approach the particular resting place in the land of Kha.
shortened: When thou approachest the land of Kha, drawest nigh unto it and perceivest its fragrance, arise before the tomb of the Glorious One and visit it with that which the Mighty, the All-Praised hath mentioned, and say:

The essence of fragrance that hath been diffused from the garment of the mercy of our Lord, the Most High, the All-Glorious, be upon thee, O thou who hast turned unto the Most Exalted Horizon and who hast spoken in praise of the Lord of Names in the kingdom of creation!

order.why: Attend to the salutation directed toward the martyrs of a city.
shortened: When thou desirest to visit the land of Ya and beholdest the darkness and light of that city, pause, facing towards it, and say: The resplendent Light shining from the horizon of God's mercy, and the perfumed Spirit made manifest by the command of God, Lord of all beings, be upon you, O company of martyrs and dawning-places of submission in the realm of creation and sources of resignation before the faces of the enemies.

order.why: Read the blessing on a body that endured hardship.
Hear the intimate greeting to a martyr’s dust.
shortened: O unique, peerless, and glorious martyr! I salute your pure dust and your holy, blessed, and fragrant resting place through the holy breaths that waft over you from the Supreme Concourse and the lights that fall upon you from the Abha Kingdom and the rainfall that perfumes your expansive precinct.

order.why: Follow light from the Kingdom toward the resting place.
shortened: Greet ye that luminous tomb and that pure and sanctified resting-place and say: "May the resplendent light shedding from the Realm of Glory and the ray shining from the Abha Kingdom envelop thy sweet-smelling mausoleum and spark upon thy resting-place that is fragrant with ambergris.

order.why: Keep Samandar’s individual remembrance and its soaring imagery.
shortened: May the fragrant breeze and the musk-laden perfume wafting from the Abha Paradise pass over your illumined grave and your perfumed tomb, O Samandar, O white falcon, O greatest eagle soaring to the heights!

order.why: Connect the community’s gladness with reverent remembrance.
shortened: By God the True One, hearts love you, breasts are gladdened by your remembrance, and souls are stirred by praise of you. God's mercy be upon one who visits your grave, God's aid be upon one who walks in the vicinity of your resting place and shows humility, submission and reverence at your tomb, for the sake of God, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.

order.why: Read communion with God at the tombs.
shortened: May God have mercy on one who visits your tombs like palaces and seeks blessings at your resting places enfolded in robes of light, who communes there with his Lord, the Mighty, the All-Forgiving, and wishes for your radiant blessings upon every patient and grateful servant.

order.why: Keep the imagery of light surrounding sacrifice.
shortened: The Light radiating from the Most Glorious Kingdom and the Beam shining forth from the Supreme Concourse. May it encompass your uttermost Tree and your furthest Tree, and may it encircle your radiant, pure, and brilliant tomb whose precincts are perfumed, for you hastened to the place of sacrifice in the path of your Beloved, the Luminary of the highest horizon.

order.why: Hear the address through fragrance and praise.
shortened: The holy fragrance and the human essence from the thicket of praise and the blessed, spacious garden, the circumambulation point of the people of Baha, has wafted over you and perfumed your pure tomb and your fragrant dust, O you who turned to God, who was attracted to the beauty of God, who was illumined by the lights of God, who received bounty from the Kingdom of God, who was martyred in the path of God, and who was slain in the love of God.

order.why: Consider the visitor moved by the remembered martyrdom.
shortened: Blessed is the one who visits you and draws near to your grave and seeks blessing from your remembrance and is moved by your martyrdom. And greetings and praise be upon you so long as the breeze continues to blow from the source of God's bounty.

order.why: Distinguish bodily reverence from its stated submission to God.
shortened: Mercy be upon him who falls prostrate upon thy dust in submission to God, and grace be upon him who circles round thy spot in humility before the Lord of Grandeur. My spirit be a sacrifice for thee, and upon thee be greetings and praise.

order.why: Remember the place where a life was given.
shortened: May the brilliant, radiant light from the Kingdom of existence envelope that spot whereupon thy pure blood was shed and where thy luminous, blessed spirit was poured forth.

order.why: Read rain and successive light as images of mercy.
Let the blessing encompass spirit, body and grave.
